recipes.name: Mandarin Chicken Pasta Salad
ingredients_raw: 1 (1 ounce) package dry onion soup mix
1 teaspoon finely chopped, peeled fresh ginger
1 (11 ounce) can mandarin orange segments, drained
0.5 cucumber - scored, halved lengthwise, seeded, and sliced

steps.text: Whisk vinegar, orange juice, vegetable oil, soup mix, sugar, sesame oil, ginger, and garlic together in a bowl until well blended; cover vinaigrette and refrigerate.

Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Cook bow tie pasta at a boil, stirring occasionally, until tender yet firm to the bite, 8 to 10 minutes. Drain and rinse under cold water. Transfer to large bowl.
Toss chicken, mandarin oranges, tomatoes, spinach, carrot, cucumber, bell pepper, onion, and almonds with pasta. Add vinaigrette: toss to coat.

raw_recipe.headline: Mandarin Chicken Pasta Salad
raw_recipe.description: This easy Mandarin chicken pasta salad recipe showcases bright and bold Asian flavors with mandarin oranges, fresh ginger, rice vinegar, and sesame oil.

review.reviewBody: Hi Shelby, I agree I don't like to use the onion soup mix either. I searched and found a homemade version here is is.. 3/4 cup dried minced onion 1/3 cup NO MSG beef bouillon powder 4 tsp onion powder 1/4 tsp celery salt 1/4 tsp sugar Directions Combine all ingredients. You can store it in a ziplock bag or air-tight container. It keeps for quite a while.

I make this regularly, this is "WOW!" if done right. A helpful summary of tips: 
First and foremost definitely use 1/3 cup of reviewer Debbie's homemade onion soup mix (a batch includes: 3/4 c minced onion, 1/3 no MSG beef bouillon powder (low salt also if possible, I use Epicure's), a heaping Tbsp onion powder, 1/4 tsp celery salt, 1/4 tsp sugar; the unused remainder stores well in an airtight container). I use this for homemade veggie dips all the time too!
Secondly, at least double the sesame oil, ginger, garlic, sugar in the dressing, to your tastes. Also use orange juice concentrate instead of OJ itself. This all gives the dressing a more intense flavour, which is needed. The original recipe is a bit bland as written. You can use red pepper flakes if you would like a kick to it.
This salad tastes better on day 2. 
Refrigerate at least for 4-5 hours before serving to allow flavours to meld, but don't add the leafy greens until just before serving so they aren't wilted.
I try to use whole grain pasta if I can find WG bowtie for better nutrition. I usually serve this as a side dish so I don't include chicken usually. Sometimes I add other veggies like broccoli instead of spinach. 
I can only give 4 stars as written but this is so worth making!!!

I thought this salad was awesome and delicious. I did use 2 more cloves of garlic, and to make the chicken more flavorful....I marinated 2 chicken breast in about 1/2 cup of the salad dressing for 6 hours then grilled on the bbq. My fiancee absolutely loved the complex flavors that this salad had, and is great on its own due to the mix of ingredients. Will definitely make again.

This was delicious. I made a few modifications based on what I had on hand. I used shell pasta, a 50/50 spring mix/spinach, left out the bell pepper and tomatoes (hubby hates raw tomatoes) and used fresh-squeezed Honeybell orange juice and another honeybell orange peeled, segmented and sliced and used a vidalia onion instead of red. I also added 2 slices of thick cut bacon (diced and browned), toasted the almonds in the bacon fat and drained, then cooked the chicken cubes (lightly seasoned with salt, pepper and powdered ginger) in the bacon fat with about a tablespoon of diced onion, then deglazed the pan with about 1/8 cup of the fresh oj. I then added the chicken/onion mixture to the dressing and refrigerated for about 3 hours. Tossed it all together when it was serving time. Hubby went back for seconds and I actually ate raw onion. I think the only change I’ll make is to use green onions and add halved cherry tomatoes next time. It does make a lot, so use a big bowl. Thanks for sharing. I can see this being a crowd-pleaser.

I thought this salad was awesome and delicious. I did use 2 more cloves of garlic, and to make the chicken more flavorful....I marinated 2 chicken breast in about 1/2 cup of the salad dressing for 6 hours then grilled on the bbq. My fiancee absolutely loved the complex flavors that this salad had, and is great on its own due to the mix of ingredients. Will definitely make again.

Excellent. Definitely a keeper. I make a lot of salads and this has become a much requested favorite. Family, including picky men, and friends love it! Holds up for a couple of days too if you keep the dressing separate. I've made it several times. My "go faster" tweaks are: Use Dole fruit cup mandarin oranges, rotisserie chicken (I always buy rotisserie chickens, pull the meat off, and freeze in freezer bags - 2 quart sized bags per chicken - so I have chicken available), use pre-shredded carrots, and use the copycat Lipton Onion Dry Soup mix recipe on this site when I don't have the packages. Making this now to take to a friend in the hospital. Thanks for this great recipe!

We make this salad several times during the summer. Only changes I made was omit the veg oil an replace with 1/8 c of Olive oil. Also, I dont add the dressing until it is ready to serve. Dressing is made the night before.

Made this for a luncheon and received great reviews. However,the spinach did not hold up for serving the next day. If the salad is not being served immediately, I recommend the spinach be added just before serving. You might also prepare all the ingredients and the dressing ahead of time, then combine just before serving.

Made as written and something was missing. I checked a couple other other recipes and found they called for 2 tablespoons soy sauce and 1 tablespoon toasted sesame seeds. Sure enough that really kicked it up to an Asian dressing.

This is a wonderful, wonderful recipe! I made it for my cooking group and they went back for seconds (even though dessert was beckoning them). I tried with powdered ginger, and it just wasn't as good. Finely mince the ginger and red pepper and definitely let the dressing 'cure' in the frig for a few hours.

This salad was delicious, filling and healthy. The only changes I made included using Rotisserie chicken (for convenience) and substituting pine nuts for the toasted almonds - more costly but worth the extra money in giving it that WOW factor. Tastes even better the second and third day. I highly recommend letting the dressing sit for 24 hours. Perfect for dinner or lunch. One of my favorite recipes on this site.
Something that we are going to do next time is double the chicken, but overall it was really good!

My husband loves this salad. I like the fact that It's a complete meal, starch, protein and veggies, great for summer suppers, and it keeps well for a few days in the fridge. I wish it didn't have so many ingredients, because I always seem to forget something, but that's a quibble.

This was an absolute great use of leftover lThanksgiving turkey! I cut the recipe in half but followed proportions exactly. To make even tastier I will double garlic next time and when using chicken breasts, I will do as other viewers suggest and marinate them in either orange juice (maybe use juice from canned mandarins as part) or some of the dressing. My husband doesn’t eat spinach or almonds, so I put the spinach on the bottom and almonds on the top of mine.
I made this today for a pool party luncheon. It was absolutely delicious and everyone raved about it. The dressing is perfect for this.

This is a fabulous recipe! The only substitution I made was instead of sliced almonds I roasted pine nuts and sprinkled on top, as my husband hates almonds. It was delicious! The homemade dressing is perfect as written!
I made it as per instructions and it was a very delicious salad. One I will make again.

This dish was amazing. As I diced everything up I separated it into bags so that I wouldn’t waste a thing. I don’t like dry onion mix but as the other viewers suggested I followed the recipe exactly. So glad I did… This is a winner and would be a show boat for company. I think next time I will top with rice noodle to give it a little crunch. Thank you so much Katrinp for sharing this recipe. PS: The reason I separated everything is so that I didn’t have to eat it all in one sitting…
The ingredients for the salad were good for a potluck dish, not a dinner salad. The dressing needed more sugar. Too tart. With the full package of onion soup l thought it would be too salty. Not so.
It was a nice salad for hot day. However the dressing is bland. Overall say it was not worth the effort given the extensive prep time.
